request.system:
You explain a fitted credit-risk model to a credit risk manager who is not a data scientist. You receive the facts about one model and write a short explanation of what drives its predictions of default.

# The text

- Write 5 to 8 sentences in plain English, most important drivers first.
- Mention an interaction when it matters for the model's predictions.
- Say only what the facts support. Do not round a weak effect up to a strong one, and do not add knowledge about credit risk that the facts do not show.
- When the facts do not settle something, say so ("the data do not settle whether ...") or leave it out.

# The answer

Return one JSON object with one list, `sentences`, each with an `id` (1, 2, 3, ...) and its `text`.
messages:
These are the facts about the model.

Model: an explainable boosting machine (EBM), fitted to predict whether a credit applicant defaults (5,000 applicants). Effects are on the log-odds scale: positive values raise the risk of default. Every band is a 95% band from 100 refits of the model on resampled data.

Features, in the order of their share of the model's importance:
- `utilization`: revolving credit utilization: the share of the credit limit in use (0 to 1).
  Share of importance 39.8% (95% band 32.1% to 46.1%); rank 1 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): x < 0.3: -0.483; 0.3 <= x < 0.628: 0; 0.628 <= x < 0.744: +1.31955; x >= 0.744: +2.57 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +3.00, 95% band [+2.56, +3.46]).
- `n_delinquencies`: number of past delinquencies on the credit file (0 to 6).
  Share of importance 23.8% (95% band 16.6% to 26.7%); rank 2 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): 0: -0.4; >= 1: +0.3 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +1.03, 95% band [+0.66, +1.20]).
- `dti`: debt-to-income ratio (0 to 0.6).
  Share of importance 10.0% (95% band 5.1% to 13.3%); rank 3 to 5 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): rises by 0.36 (95% band [+0.15, +0.56]) from x = 0.0312 (5th percentile) to x = 0.571 (95th percentile); the shape in between is not resolved at this sample size.
- `income`: annual income in US dollars.
  Share of importance 7.6% (95% band 4.1% to 10.5%); rank 3 to 6 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): falls by 0.48 (95% band [-0.74, -0.23]) from x = 21,800 (5th percentile) to x = 111,000 (95th percentile); the shape in between is not resolved at this sample size.
- `history_months`: length of the credit history in months.
  Share of importance 7.1% (95% band 2.1% to 9.9%); rank 3 to 7 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): falls by 0.34 (95% band [-0.59, -0.04]) from x = 23.8 (5th percentile) to x = 343 (95th percentile); the shape in between is not resolved at this sample size.
- `months_at_address`: months at the current address (standardised).
  Share of importance 2.6% (95% band 0.8% to 6.3%); rank 4 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile -0.11, 95% band [-0.27, +0.13]).
- `num_dependents`: number of dependents (standardised).
  Share of importance 1.6% (95% band 0.4% to 4.8%); rank 5 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile -0.04, 95% band [-0.36, +0.14]).
- `age`: age of the applicant in years.
  Share of importance 0.7% (95% band 0.5% to 5.6%); rank 5 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.04, 95% band [-0.10, +0.32]).
- `n_inquiries`: number of recent credit inquiries.
  Share of importance 0.3% (95% band 0.0% to 3.5%); rank 6 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.03, 95% band [-0.00, +0.29]).

Interactions: the model has 5 pairs. The larger ones:
- `history_months & num_dependents`: share of importance 1.7% (95% band 0.0% to 4.7%).
  Effect of `history_months` from 23.8 to 343: -0.52 (95% band -1.00 to -0.07) when `num_dependents` = -1.65, -0.17 (95% band -0.52 to +0.21) when `num_dependents` = 1.59.
  Effect of `num_dependents` from -1.65 to 1.59: -0.20 (95% band -0.65 to +0.08) when `history_months` = 23.8, +0.14 (95% band -0.28 to +0.51) when `history_months` = 343.
- `dti & months_at_address`: share of importance 1.7% (95% band 0.0% to 3.9%).
  Effect of `dti` from 0.0312 to 0.571: +0.54 (95% band +0.16 to +1.03) when `months_at_address` = -1.64, +0.22 (95% band -0.22 to +0.46) when `months_at_address` = 1.64.
  Effect of `months_at_address` from -1.64 to 1.64: +0.04 (95% band -0.19 to +0.41) when `dti` = 0.0312, -0.28 (95% band -0.71 to +0.10) when `dti` = 0.571.
- `dti & num_dependents`: share of importance 1.7% (95% band 0.0% to 3.8%).
  Effect of `dti` from 0.0312 to 0.571: +0.40 (95% band +0.15 to +0.66) when `num_dependents` = -1.65, +0.26 (95% band -0.04 to +0.55) when `num_dependents` = 1.59.
  Effect of `num_dependents` from -1.65 to 1.59: +0.04 (95% band -0.33 to +0.26) when `dti` = 0.0312, -0.10 (95% band -0.45 to +0.14) when `dti` = 0.571.
- `income & months_at_address`: share of importance 0.9% (95% band 0.0% to 2.5%).
  Effect of `income` from 21,800 to 111,000: -0.51 (95% band -0.74 to -0.18) when `months_at_address` = -1.64, -0.55 (95% band -0.83 to -0.24) when `months_at_address` = 1.64.
  Effect of `months_at_address` from -1.64 to 1.64: -0.03 (95% band -0.26 to +0.32) when `income` = 21,800, -0.07 (95% band -0.28 to +0.18) when `income` = 111,000.
- 1 further pairs with a share below 0.5% each, together 0.5%.

Write the explanation.

content.text: {"sentences":[{"id":1,"text":"The model's predictions of default are driven mainly by revolving credit utilization, which accounts for about 40% of its importance, with a plausible range of roughly 32% to 46%."},{"id":2,"text":"Applicants using 74% or more of their credit limit carry a much higher predicted risk of default, with the effect rising from about -0.5 at low utilization to about +2.6 at high utilization on the log-odds scale, a net swing of about +3.0."},{"id":3,"text":"The second most important driver is the number of past delinquencies: having any delinquency on file raises predicted risk, with a net effect of about +1.0 log-odds between typical low and high values, though the band on that effect is fairly wide."},{"id":4,"text":"Debt-to-income ratio, annual income and length of credit history each matter to a lesser degree (roughly 7% to 10% of importance), with higher debt-to-income and lower income and shorter credit history each pushing predicted risk up."},{"id":5,"text":"Months at address, number of dependents, age and recent credit inquiries show no effect that the data can distinguish from zero, so they should not be read as drivers of the predictions."},{"id":6,"text":"There are some interactions, but they are small and their ranges are wide: the effect of debt-to-income appears stronger for applicants with fewer dependents and shorter time at their address, and the effect of credit history is weaker for applicants with more dependents."},{"id":7,"text":"The data do not settle how large these interactions really are, so they should be treated as tentative rather than as established features of the model."}]}
